newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Fletcher Energy starts new oil well.
newsitem.headline: Fletcher Energy starts new oil well.

text.p: Fletcher Challenge Energy on Monday said it had commenced drilling of the Manu-1 well -- the first in a programme that will explore for oil and gas under five onshore exploration licences acquired in December 1995 in the Taranaki region of New Zealand's North Island.
The well was spudded at at 7.30 a.m. on Saturday.
Manu-1 is located close to the producing TAWN field in the onshore Taranaki Basin - 3 km south of the Tariki field and two km north of the Ahuroa field.
These fields contain combined original reserves of 95 billion standard cubic feet of gas and 3.5 million barrels of associated condensate liquid hydrocarbons.
Manu-1 is 10 km north of the Waihapa field, which contains original reserves of approximately 28 million barrels of oil and associated gas.

The principal objectives in the Manu-1 well are the fractured Tikorangi Limestone, which has produced oil from the Waihapa/Ngaere field, and the Tariki Sandstone which is currently producing gas into the recently commissioned TAWN gas treatment plant.
The targeted depth of the Manu-1 well is 3,750 metres and drilling time is estimated at 46 days.
The onshore programme is in addition to two recently announced wells, being drilled by the Sedco 703 semi submersible rig, as part of the programme being undertaken offshore Taranaki.
The first of these, Awatea -1, is currently being drilled 55 kilometres west of Kawhia, in the northern part of the Taranaki Basin. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 4734 746
